title: Peggy Flanagan Wins Big in Minnesota Primary
summary: Have you ever heard of a primary? It's an election where each party picks its candidate for the big election. In Minnesota, something exciting happened on Tuesday. Peggy Flanagan won the Democratic primary for the U.S. Senate. She beat Angie Craig, who was backed by many big-name Democrats like Nancy Pelosi. Flanagan is a progressive, which means she wants big changes. She says she'll fight against the influence of corporations and stand up to President Trump. At her victory party, she said, "This campaign was about the many versus the money. Well guess what? The many just won!" That means regular people beat big money. Flanagan is now the front-runner to win the Senate seat in November. Her opponent will be Michele Tafoya, a former NFL sideline reporter. Minnesota hasn't elected a Republican to statewide office since 2006, so Flanagan has a good chance. But Republicans hope a scandal about stolen public money will help them. Flanagan got support from popular progressives like Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren. She also highlighted that Craig voted for a controversial immigration bill that became unpopular after immigration agents shot and killed two people in Minneapolis. Flanagan says she doesn't take money from big corporations or AIPAC, a group that supports Israel. One supporter said, "I love that she doesn't take any corporate money." So now, all eyes are on the general election in November. Will Flanagan win? We'll have to wait and see!
why_it_matters: Primaries decide who gets to compete for office, and those winners help make rules about schools, jobs, and daily life that can affect your family.

AIPAC (a group in Washington that supports Israel) works to influence U.S. politics, and Flanagan says she does not take its money.
